summary: Phase 2 — P1 (UI surfaces) + P2 (persisted prediction history) verified end-to-end against the live public preview. Backend: added /app/backend/tests/test_prediction_history_endpoint.py (10 tests, 10/10 PASS in 36.2s) covering (a) auth gating on GET /api/prediction/history (401/403 without/with bad token), (b) history populated after GET /api/prediction with full row schema {prediction_id, predicted_period_start, cycle_length_prediction, confidence, reliability_score, reliability_classification, data_sufficiency_level, model_weights, engine_version, generated_at, updated_at} and validationMetrics.metrics has {mae,rmse,success_rate,stability_score,samples} (samples=3, mae=0, rmse=0, success_rate=100 for 12 regular 28d cycles), (c) idempotency — six repeated GET /api/prediction?today=2025-06-01 calls keep history.count flat (deterministic prediction_id upsert via unique index user_id+prediction_id is working), (d) ?limit=1 respected — after a second prediction with extra cycle history.count grows, but ?limit=1 returns exactly 1 row, (e) outlierClassifications entries surface BOTH 'type' and 'outlier_type' with the same value (verified via 5-day gap inducing 'Logging Error' alias). Regression: prior /app/backend/tests/test_prediction_v2_endpoint.py still 13/13 PASS in 48.9s — GET /api/prediction is still 200 with engineVersion 2.0.0 + every v2 field; /api/dashboard, /api/daily-summary, /api/analytics still 200. Frontend (mobile viewport 390x844, demo@cycle.app/DemoPass123!, /insights): every required testID renders — prediction-window-card, prediction-reliability-card (with prediction-reliability ring + prediction-reliability-score='69' + prediction-reliability-chip='Moderate'), prediction-intervals-card (rows prediction-interval-p50/p75/p90/p95 all present with monotonic ±2d/±4d/±8d/±16d half-widths), prediction-prob-card, prediction-fertile-card. Confidence displays as a rounded integer percentage '56%' (Math.round applied in PredictionPanel.tsx:148, no decimals). prediction-data-sufficiency is absent — expected, demo user has 13 cycles (sufficiency level 4) so the cold-start note is intentionally hidden by the `level < 4` guard (PredictionPanel.tsx:164). No console errors, no React Native red screen, no broken images. NOTE: One non-blocking observation — PredictionPanel.tsx is 555 lines, hovering the 700-line code-review threshold; splitting into sub-files (ReliabilityRing, IntervalBands, ProbabilityCurve, FertileBar) would improve maintainability if the file grows further.
critical_code_review_comments: PredictionPanel.tsx is 555 lines — close to the 700-line refactor threshold. Consider extracting ReliabilityRing, IntervalBands, ProbabilityCurve and FertileBar into separate files (e.g. /app/frontend/src/components/prediction/*.tsx). Non-blocking for this iteration.

/api/prediction/history rows include 'algorithm_version' and 'predicted_period_start' but NOT 'predictedDate'/'algorithmVersion' (camelCase) — naming style differs from the /api/prediction response (which is camelCase throughout). The history endpoint is consistent within itself (snake_case persisted shape) and the review request explicitly enumerates snake_case keys, so this is intentional, but worth documenting for downstream consumers who hit both endpoints.

Persistence in /api/prediction is wrapped in a broad try/except that logs but never propagates — good for read availability, but if Mongo silently fails for a long time the history endpoint will go empty without any user-visible signal. Consider a counter/health gauge in a follow-up.

outlierClassifications now carries both 'type' and 'outlier_type' — the v1 audit-trail change-points list ALSO uses a key called 'type' (with values 'increase'/'decrease'), and trend_adjustments entries have a 'type' too. These coexist in different sub-objects so there is no collision, but a downstream client doing a flat key scan could confuse them. Documenting the alias as 'outlier-only' would help.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all required testIDs render, confidence formatted as rounded integer)

seed_data_creation: Each new history-endpoint test registers its own fresh user (via conftest register_user → DEV email mode reads codes from /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log) and seeds cycles via POST /api/cycles. No persistent fixtures left behind. The demo@cycle.app account was used READ-ONLY for the frontend run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: P2 persistence is wired via Mongo collections db.prediction_history (unique index user_id+prediction_id, upsert keyed on prediction_id which is a deterministic sha256 of cycle starts/ends — NOT of `today`, so calling /api/prediction with different `today` params on the same cycle history yields the SAME prediction_id and the SAME single row) and db.validation_metrics (unique user_id, single-row snapshot). The new GET /api/prediction/history?limit=N returns {history:[...], count, validationMetrics}; rows are sorted by updated_at DESC and `_id` is stripped. To force a new history row, mutate the cycle history (add/edit/delete a cycle). The outlierClassifications 'type' alias was added in prediction_engine_v2.py:167 ('type': otype, 'outlier_type': otype, ...). On the UI, prediction-data-sufficiency only renders when dataSufficiency.level < 4 (PredictionPanel.tsx:164) — the demo user already has 13 cycles so this card is hidden by design; to surface it, test with a fresh user that has <6 cycles.
